comments.text: The creator of the video seems confused at what the paper is saying. To clarify, doctor agents can’t learn from simulation and then apply to the real world because simulation cannot replicate the biochemical processes of the human body today. The whole study is simply showing we can make the database table “experience base”  look equal to “golden answers” over time by having LLM churn through it.  Of course a more efficient way to teach the agent is to feed the LLM model the golden answers to begin with.  It also seems they are using vector database for retrieval which would stop working after X rounds of adding new learning experiences unless there’s some sort of junk data clean up.  Ideally fine tuning would be used but probably wouldn’t work with LLM produced data at this time, hard to say.   (I’m a doctor and a ai software engineer)
